parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is labelled presentation because it matches the **/*.module.ts pattern. A NestJS module of this kind should only wire controllers, providers and imports together. This one also holds real logic. In MulterModule.registerAsync's useFactory, it sets up disk storage: a fixed destination ('./files') and a filename generator that builds a random string plus the lowercased original extension. That is file-storage logic, which belongs in the infrastructure layer. It also holds an upload policy, the fileFilter that only allows jpg, jpeg, png and gif and rejects anything else with an UnprocessableEntityException. That is a business or validation rule that belongs in an application service or validation component, not in module wiring. Choosing between the document and relational persistence modules based on databaseConfig().isDocumentDatabase is normal wiring and is acceptable. Treating Nest modules as composition roots could justify the storage setup, which is why confidence is moderate.
